questions.stem: Estimate the mass of the galaxy NGC 6946 actually present in the picture in Fig. 1(A).
questions.answer: The mass embedded in a sphere of radius $r$ is given by $M_{\text{int}} = \int_0^r 4\pi x^2 \rho_m(x) dx = 4\pi C_m \left[r - r_m \arctan\left(\frac{r}{r_m}\right)\right]$, which reduces to $M_{\text{int}} \simeq 4\pi C_m r$ if $r \gg r_m$. In the picture we have a radius $R = 9 \text{ kpc} = 2.27 \times 10^{20} \text{ m}$ of the galaxy, then a mass $M_{\text{in the figure}} \simeq 4\pi C_m R \simeq 10^{41} \text{ kg} \simeq 10^{11} M_{\odot}$.

questions.stem: Find the equation of motion on $z$ for the vertical motion of a point mass $m$ in such a potential, assuming $r$ is constant. Show that, if $r < r_0$, the galactic plane is a stable equilibrium state by giving the angular frequency $\omega_0$ of small oscillations around it.
questions.answer: The gravitational potential is given by $\varphi_G(r, z) = \varphi_0 \ln\left(\frac{r}{r_0}\right) \exp\left(-\frac{z^2}{z_0^2}\right)$. The equation of motion for $z$ is derived from the force $F_z = -m \frac{\partial \varphi_G}{\partial z} = m \frac{2 \varphi_0 z}{z_0^2} \ln\left(\frac{r}{r_0}\right) \exp\left(-\frac{z^2}{z_0^2}\right)$. For small oscillations around $z = 0$, the potential can be approximated as harmonic, leading to an angular frequency $\omega_0 = \sqrt{\frac{2 \varphi_0}{z_0^2} \ln\left(\frac{r_0}{r}\right)}$.

questions.stem: In our galaxy, 𝑣⊙ = 220 km ⋅ s−1. Determine the values of the relative radial velocity (with 3 significant digits) and the distance from the galactic center (with 2 significant digits) of the 3 sources observed in Fig. 3. Distances should be expressed as multiples of 𝑅⊙.
questions.answer:
The 3 frequency shifts (𝑓 − 𝑓0) corresponding to each peak are 𝛥𝑓1 = 0.03 MHz, 𝛥𝑓2 = 0.15 MHz, and 𝛥𝑓3 = 0.26 MHz. The relative Doppler velocities are calculated using 𝑣𝑟,𝑖 = 𝑐𝛥𝑓𝑖/𝑓0, with 𝑓0 = 1,420 MHz, resulting in:
• 𝑣𝑟,1 = 6.33 km ⋅ s−1
• 𝑣𝑟,2 = 31.7 km ⋅ s−1
• 𝑣𝑟,3 = 54.9 km ⋅ s−1
The corresponding distances from the galactic center are obtained using the relation 𝑅𝑖 = 𝑅⊙ / (1 + (𝑣𝑟,𝑖 / 𝑣⊙) sin ℓ), with ℓ = 30°, resulting in:
• 𝑅1 = 0.95𝑅⊙
• 𝑅2 = 0.78𝑅⊙
• 𝑅3 = 0.67𝑅⊙

questions.stem: On the top view of our galaxy (in the answer box), indicate the positions of the sources observed in Fig. 3. What could be deduced from repeated measurements changing ℓ?
questions.answer: The positions of the sources can be indicated geometrically using the 15° grid graduation, going back from 30° from the perpendicular line to CS. The line of sight is passing by S and is tangent to the circle of radius CS/2. Drawing the circles of radius 𝑅1, 𝑅2, and 𝑅3, the line of sight with ℓ = 30° gives 2 possible intersections for each peak: a near one and a far one. Only the nearest for each source is plotted on the answer figure. From repeated measurements changing ℓ, one could deduce the distribution and motion of sources in the galaxy.
